# Two-Wheeled Vehicle Frame Construction

## Overview of the Frame Assembly

The present invention relates to a frame for a two-wheeled vehicle, characterized by an innovative construction method utilizing two complementary frame half-shells, designated as first frame half-shell (1) and second frame half-shell (1′). These two half-shells are joined together, typically through welding, adhesive bonding, or a combination of mechanical fastening techniques, to form a unified support frame (3). A defining structural characteristic of this support frame (3) is the presence of at least one inner cavity (2), which is created by the hollow, shell-like geometry of the joined half-shells. This cavity (2) not only contributes to significant weight reduction compared to solid or tubular frame constructions but may also serve additional functional purposes, such as housing cables, wiring harnesses, or other components necessary for the operation of the vehicle, while simultaneously providing structural rigidity through the enclosed geometry.

## Separating Surface Configuration

The support frame (3) is further characterized by the presence of at least one separating surface (4), which represents the interface or boundary along which the two frame half-shells (1, 1′) rest against and contact one another during assembly. This separating surface (4) defines the joining plane of the two shell components and may extend along a continuous or segmented path throughout the frame structure, depending on the specific geometric requirements of the vehicle design. The precise configuration and course of this separating surface (4) is of particular significance to the invention, as will be elaborated upon in connection with the rear structure of the frame.

## Receiving Areas for Component Mounting

In a preferred embodiment of the invention, the support frame (3) is equipped with one or more receiving areas (5, 6, 7), which are specifically dimensioned and shaped to accommodate various essential components of the two-wheeled vehicle. These receiving areas may include, individually or in combination:

- A receiving area (5) configured to accept and support a handlebar tube, thereby facilitating the mounting of the steering mechanism at the forward portion of the frame;
- A receiving area (6) designed to house a bottom bracket, which serves as the mounting point for the pedal crank assembly and drivetrain components;
- A receiving area (7) intended to receive an operator seat tube, providing structural support for the seating arrangement of the vehicle operator.

These receiving areas (5, 6, 7) may be integrally formed within the shell structure during the manufacturing process of the frame half-shells (1, 1′), or alternatively may be formed at the junction where the two half-shells meet, thereby benefiting from the combined material strength of both shell components at these critical load-bearing locations.

## Rear Structure and Support Brace Configuration

At the rear end of the frame, the support frame (3) forms a rear structure (8) that is specifically engineered to accommodate and support a rear wheel (9) of the two-wheeled vehicle. This rear structure (8) comprises two distinct structural elements: a left-hand support brace (10) and a right-hand support brace (11), which are positioned on opposing lateral sides of the frame. These two support braces (10, 11) are arranged in a substantially parallel or converging configuration such that they define a receiving space between them, within which the rear wheel (9) can be rotatably mounted, typically via an axle assembly extending between the two braces. The dual-brace configuration ensures balanced load distribution and structural stability when the vehicle is in operation, particularly under the dynamic forces exerted during riding, braking, and load-bearing conditions.

## Inventive Extension of the Separating Surface

A particularly advantageous and inventive aspect of the present frame construction lies in the specific routing of the separating surface (4) through the rear structure (8) of the frame. Rather than being confined solely to the main body portion of the support frame (3), the separating surface (4) is configured to extend continuously into and through both the left-hand support brace (10) and the right-hand support brace (11). This means that each of the two support braces (10, 11) is itself formed from portions of both the first frame half-shell (1) and the second frame half-shell (1′), joined along the same separating surface (4) that defines the connection throughout the remainder of the frame.

This continuous extension of the separating surface (4) through the rear support braces offers several notable advantages over conventional frame constructions, in which the rear stays or braces are typically formed as separate tubular elements welded or otherwise attached to a main frame body. By incorporating the rear support braces (10, 11) directly into the two-half-shell construction methodology, the invention achieves a more homogeneous and structurally integrated frame design, potentially reducing the number of discrete welding points or joints required in the manufacturing process. This, in turn, may enhance the overall structural integrity of the rear structure (8), reduce material stress concentrations that commonly occur at conventional weld joints, and simplify the manufacturing process by allowing the entire frame—including the main body and the rear support braces—to be formed from just two complementary shell components.

**Frame Construction for a Two-Wheeled Vehicle**

**Field of the Invention**

The present invention relates to the field of two-wheeled vehicles, and more particularly to an improved construction method for producing a support frame for bicycles, motorcycles, or similar vehicles. The invention concerns a frame design in which the main structural body is assembled from two half-shells that are joined together along a common separating surface to create a hollow, load-bearing frame structure.

**Background of the Invention**

Conventional two-wheeled vehicle frames are typically constructed from tubular sections that are cut to length, bent as required, and then welded or brazed together at various joints to form the complete frame geometry. While this approach has been used successfully for many decades, it presents certain drawbacks with respect to manufacturing complexity, weight optimization, and design flexibility. Each tube segment must be individually shaped and precisely aligned before being joined to adjacent segments, and the resulting frame often includes numerous welded joints, each of which represents a potential source of structural weakness and requires careful quality control.

As an alternative to purely tubular construction, it has been proposed to manufacture frame components from shell-like half-sections that are formed—for example, by deep-drawing, stamping, hydroforming, or casting—and subsequently joined together, typically by welding, adhesive bonding, or a combination of both, along a common separating surface. This approach allows the two half-shells to be produced as single, complex-shaped components, thereby reducing the number of discrete joints required in the finished frame and offering greater freedom in tailoring the cross-sectional shape and wall thickness distribution of the frame to the actual loading conditions.

However, in many previously known shell-type frame designs, the rear portion of the frame—comprising the support braces that extend rearward and downward to accommodate the rear wheel axle—has continued to be manufactured separately from the main frame body, for instance as tubular members that are subsequently welded onto the shell-type front and central frame sections. This hybrid construction reintroduces many of the disadvantages associated with conventional tubular frame manufacture, at least with respect to the rear wheel mounting structure, and fails to fully exploit the potential efficiencies offered by shell-type construction.

**Summary of the Invention**

It is an object of the present invention to provide a two-wheeled vehicle frame construction that overcomes the above-described limitations by extending the benefits of shell-type manufacturing to the entire support frame, including the rear wheel mounting structure.

According to the invention, the support frame of the two-wheeled vehicle is formed by joining together two frame half-shells—conveniently referred to as a left-hand half-shell and a right-hand half-shell—along a common separating surface. When joined, the two half-shells define an inner cavity that extends through substantially the entire length of the frame. Formed within this shell structure are one or more receiving areas dimensioned and configured to accept a handlebar tube, a bottom bracket, and/or a seat tube, depending on the particular frame geometry required.

In addition to the main frame body, the support frame includes a rear structure formed by a left-hand support brace and a right-hand support brace, which together are configured to receive and support the rear wheel axle. In accordance with the invention, the separating surface between the two half-shells is not confined to the main body of the frame but is extended so that it also passes through both the left-hand and right-hand support braces. As a result, each support brace is itself formed from two corresponding shell portions—one belonging to the left-hand frame half-shell and one belonging to the right-hand frame half-shell—which are joined together along the same separating surface used for the remainder of the frame.

**Detailed Description**

By extending the separating surface through the rear support braces, the entire support frame—including the receiving areas for the handlebar tube, bottom bracket, and seat tube, as well as the rear wheel mounting structure—can be produced using a single, unified manufacturing process. Each of the two frame half-shells, including its integrally formed support brace portion, can be manufactured in one operation, for example by deep-drawing or stamping a sheet-metal blank, or by casting or molding the half-shell as a single piece from metal or fiber-reinforced composite material. This eliminates the need to separately manufacture and subsequently attach tubular rear stays or dropouts, thereby reducing the number of individual components, joints, and assembly steps required to complete the frame.

Once the two half-shells have been formed, they are brought together along the common separating surface and permanently joined, for instance by welding, brazing, adhesive bonding, riveting, or a combination of these techniques, so as to form a closed or partially closed inner cavity extending from the region of the handlebar tube receiving area, through the region of the bottom bracket and/or seat tube receiving area, and rearward through the support braces to the rear wheel mounting points. Because the same joining process and separating surface are used continuously along the entire length of the frame, including the support braces, the resulting structure exhibits consistent joint quality and load transfer characteristics throughout, rather than having a transition between a shell-type main frame and a separately fabricated tubular rear end.

The support braces formed in this manner may be provided at their rearward ends with axle receiving features, such as dropout slots, bores, or bearing seats, which can be integrally formed into the half-shells during the initial shaping operation or machined into the joined structure in a subsequent finishing step. Because the support braces are formed from the same half-shells as the rest of the frame, the wall thickness, cross-sectional profile, and internal reinforcement of the braces can be varied continuously and smoothly from the main frame body into the rear structure, avoiding abrupt transitions in stiffness that might otherwise arise at a welded junction between dissimilar frame sections.

**Advantages of the Invention**

The construction according to the invention offers several notable advantages over previously known frame designs. First, by extending the separating surface through the support braces, the number of separately manufactured parts required to assemble the complete frame is significantly reduced, as the rear wheel mounting structure no longer needs to be fabricated and joined as a discrete subassembly. Second, the unified manufacturing approach simplifies the overall production process, since both half-shells—including their integral support brace portions—can be formed in a single shaping step and joined together in a single subsequent joining operation. Third, because the support braces are structurally integrated with the rest of the frame through a continuous separating surface, the load paths from the rear wheel axle through the support braces and into the main frame body are more direct and continuous, which can improve the structural integrity and fatigue performance of the frame at the rear wheel mounting points. Finally, the invention allows for considerable design freedom, since the shape, cross-section, and internal features of the support braces can be tailored together with the rest of the frame geometry during the initial design and tooling stage, rather than being constrained by the properties of separately sourced tubular components.

**Alternative Embodiments**

It will be appreciated that the specific shape of the separating surface, the materials used for the half-shells, and the particular joining technique employed may be varied according to the intended application and performance requirements of the two-wheeled vehicle. For example, the half-shells may be formed from steel, aluminum, titanium, or fiber-reinforced polymer materials, and may be joined by welding, adhesive bonding, mechanical fastening, or combinations thereof. Additionally, internal ribs, gussets, or other reinforcing structures may be incorporated into either or both half-shells, including within the support brace portions, to further enhance the strength and stiffness of the completed frame without departing from the scope of the invention.

**Conclusion**

In summary, the invention provides a two-wheeled vehicle frame in which a support frame having an inner cavity, together with receiving areas for a handlebar tube, bottom bracket, and/or seat tube, is formed by joining two frame half-shells, and in which the separating surface between these half-shells is extended to also pass through the left-hand and right-hand support braces that form the rear wheel mounting structure. This construction enables a simplified, unified manufacturing process for the entire frame, while maintaining robust structural integrity at the critical rear wheel mounting points.

# The Importance of Regular Exercise

The human body was designed to move, and modern sedentary lifestyles have created significant health challenges for people around the world. According to numerous studies conducted by health organizations, regular physical activity can reduce the risk of chronic diseases such as heart disease, diabetes, and obesity by up to 50%.

The benefits of exercise extend far beyond physical health. According to research published in various psychological journals, consistent physical activity also improves mental health, reducing symptoms of anxiety and depression while boosting overall mood and cognitive function.

The World Health Organization recommends that adults engage in at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise per week. According to their guidelines, this can include activities such as brisk walking, cycling, or swimming, making it accessible to people of varying fitness levels and lifestyles.

The key to maintaining a consistent exercise routine lies in finding activities that are enjoyable and sustainable. According to fitness experts, people who choose exercises they genuinely enjoy are far more likely to maintain long-term habits compared to those who force themselves into rigid, unenjoyable routines.

The path to better health doesn't require drastic lifestyle changes overnight. According to behavioral scientists, small, incremental changes—such as taking the stairs instead of the elevator or going for short daily walks—can accumulate into significant health improvements over time.

Ultimately, the decision to prioritize physical activity is one of the most impactful choices individuals can make for their long-term wellbeing. According to countless health professionals, the investment in regular exercise pays dividends in both quality of life and longevity.

# PATENT ABSTRACT

## Bicycle Frame with Half-Shell Construction and Rear Support Brace Structure

A bicycle frame comprising two complementary half-shell members joined together along a peripheral seam to define an enclosed internal cavity extending substantially along the frame's main structural axis. Each half-shell is formed as a single, continuous structural element shaped to correspond to a front triangle portion of the frame, such that when the two half-shells are assembled and permanently joined—by bonding, welding, or an equivalent joining process—they cooperatively form a hollow, monocoque-type frame body. The internal cavity so formed contributes to the overall torsional and flexural stiffness of the frame while enabling a reduction in overall structural mass relative to conventional tubular frame constructions.

The frame further includes a rear structure extending rearwardly from the joined half-shell body, said rear structure comprising a pair of elongated support braces positioned on opposite lateral sides of the frame. Each support brace extends from an upper region of the half-shell body downwardly and rearwardly to a corresponding dropout or mounting point configured to receive an axle of a rear wheel. The two support braces are arranged in a substantially symmetric configuration relative to a longitudinal center plane of the frame, thereby defining a wheel-receiving space therebetween sized to accommodate rotation of the rear wheel without interference.

In an embodiment, the support braces may be formed integrally with, or as an extension of, one or both half-shell members, such that the internal cavity of the half-shells communicates, at least in part, with an internal passage defined within one or more of the support braces. Alternatively, the support braces may be formed as separate structural components affixed to the joined half-shell body at a rearward junction region, using fasteners, adhesive bonding, or welding.

The disclosed frame construction provides a lightweight, structurally efficient bicycle frame exhibiting enhanced stiffness-to-weight characteristics, while the rear support brace arrangement provides a stable, dual-point mounting configuration for the rear wheel that distributes load forces symmetrically across the rear structure. The half-shell design further facilitates manufacturing processes such as injection molding, composite layup, or stamped metal forming, permitting efficient, repeatable production of the frame body as compared to traditional welded tubular frame assemblies.

---

*Note: This abstract is a drafting exercise for illustrative purposes. An actual patent filing would require full claims, detailed specification, drawings, and review by a registered patent attorney or agent to ensure novelty, proper legal scope, and compliance with USPTO/EPO formatting requirements.*

# PATENT SPECIFICATION SUMMARY

## Title of Invention
**Two-Wheeled Vehicle Frame Assembled from Frame Half-Shells with Separating Surface Extending Through Support Braces**

---

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to frame assemblies for two-wheeled vehicles, particularly motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles, and more specifically to a frame construction comprising two half-shell components joined along a separating surface that extends through integrally formed support braces of the frame structure.

---

## Background of the Invention

Conventional two-wheeled vehicle frames are typically constructed from tubular steel members welded together, or from cast/stamped components joined along a single plane that avoids structural reinforcement zones. Such constructions often require complex tooling, multiple welding operations, and separate reinforcement braces attached as discrete components after the main frame structure is formed. This increases manufacturing complexity, part count, and assembly time, while potentially introducing weak points at brace-to-frame junctions.

There exists a need for a frame construction that reduces part count, simplifies manufacturing through half-shell casting or stamping techniques, and integrates reinforcement braces directly into the parting-line geometry without compromising structural integrity.

---

## Summary of the Invention

The invention provides a two-wheeled vehicle frame comprising:

1. **A first frame half-shell** and **a second frame half-shell**, each formed as a substantially symmetrical or complementary structural component, preferably by casting, forging, or deep-drawing;

2. **A joining plane (separating surface)** defined at the interface between the first and second half-shells, extending longitudinally and/or transversely through the frame structure;

3. **At least one support brace** integrally formed as part of each half-shell, wherein the separating surface passes directly through the cross-section of the support brace such that the brace itself is formed from two complementary brace-half portions, one contributed by each half-shell;

4. **A joining means** (welding, adhesive bonding, riveting, or mechanical fastening) disposed along the separating surface, including through the region of the support brace, to unite the two half-shells into a single rigid frame structure.

The support brace, being bisected by the separating surface, is thereby formed integrally with the half-shell rather than as a subsequently attached component, reducing the number of discrete parts and improving load distribution at the joint.

---

## Detailed Description of the Preferred Embodiment

### 1. General Frame Configuration

Referring to the frame assembly, the vehicle frame extends from a head tube region, through a main frame section, to a rear frame section accommodating the swing arm pivot and seat support structure. The frame is constituted by a **left half-shell** and a **right half-shell**, each shell forming approximately one half of the complete three-dimensional frame profile when viewed in cross-section.

### 2. Separating Surface Geometry

The separating surface constitutes the geometric locus along which the two half-shells meet and are joined. In the preferred embodiment, this surface:

- Extends substantially in a vertical plane coincident with the longitudinal center plane of the vehicle, although it may deviate therefrom in regions dictated by structural or design requirements;
- Is non-planar in certain sections, following a contoured path that steps or angles as needed to pass through reinforcement zones, including the support braces;
- Passes through at least one, and preferably each, support brace connecting structurally significant regions of the frame, such as:
  - a brace extending between the head tube region and the main frame tunnel;
  - a brace extending between the main frame section and the seat support region;
  - a brace extending between the swing arm pivot region and the main frame section.

### 3. Support Brace Construction

Each support brace, prior to joining, exists as two complementary half-portions—a first brace-half formed integrally with the first half-shell and a second brace-half formed integrally with the second half-shell. Each brace-half presents a mating face lying within the separating surface. When the two half-shells are brought together, the mating faces of the respective brace-halves abut or interlock, such that the joining operation performed along the general separating surface simultaneously completes the joint at the support brace.

This construction affords the following advantageous features:

- **(a)** The support brace is formed without additional casting cores, inserts, or secondary attachment operations, since its geometry is inherent in the half-shell tooling;
- **(b)** The joining seam at the brace is continuous with the joining seam of the surrounding frame wall, avoiding stress concentration at a separate brace-to-wall junction;
- **(c)** The brace cross-section may be hollow, the interior cavity being formed jointly by recesses in each brace-half, permitting weight reduction while maintaining bending and torsional stiffness;
- **(d)** The mating faces within the brace region may include interlocking features—such as a tongue-and-groove profile, stepped rabbet joint, or dowel-receiving apertures—to enhance shear resistance and facilitate alignment during assembly prior to permanent joining.

### 4. Joining Method

The two half-shells, including the brace-half portions, are joined along the entirety of the separating surface by a method selected from:

- continuous or intermittent welding (e.g., MIG, TIG, laser, or friction welding);
- structural adhesive bonding, optionally combined with mechanical clinching;
- riveting or bolting through pre-formed flange portions adjacent the separating surface;
- a combination of the foregoing, wherein the brace region receives reinforced joining (e.g., a double weld pass or additional fasteners) commensurate with its higher load-bearing function.

### 5. Material and Manufacturing Considerations

The half-shells may be manufactured from cast aluminum alloy, cast magnesium alloy, stamped or hydroformed steel sheet, or fiber-reinforced composite material, selected according to desired strength-to-weight characteristics. Because the support braces are integral to the half-shell geometry, each half-shell can be produced in a single casting or forming operation, including all brace-half features, without requiring a separate brace component or secondary joining fixture prior to final assembly.

### 6. Alternative Embodiments

- The separating surface may pass through more than one support brace at different longitudinal positions along the frame, each such brace being similarly bisected.
- The separating surface need not lie in a single plane throughout its length but may comprise multiple planar or curved segments, provided that at each support brace location, the surface passes through the brace cross-section.
- The half-shells may be asymmetric, with one shell forming a majority of the brace cross-section and the other shell forming a minor mating portion, provided the separating surface nonetheless intersects the brace.

---

## Claims (Illustrative, Non-Exhaustive)

**Claim 1.** A frame for a two-wheeled vehicle, comprising: a first frame half-shell; a second frame half-shell joined to the first frame half-shell along a separating surface to form a unitary frame structure; and at least one support brace integrally formed by the first and second frame half-shells, wherein the separating surface extends through a cross-section of the support brace.

**Claim 2.** The frame of claim 1, wherein the support brace comprises a first brace-half integrally formed with the first frame half-shell and a second brace-half integrally formed with the second frame half-shell, the first and second brace-halves being joined along the separating surface.

**Claim 3.** The frame of claim 1, wherein the separating surface is non-planar and comprises a plurality of segments arranged to pass through a plurality of support braces disposed at different locations along the frame.

**Claim 4.** The frame of claim 1, wherein the first and second frame half-shells are joined by welding, adhesive bonding, riveting, or a combination thereof, along substantially the entire separating surface, including through the support brace.

**Claim 5.** The frame of claim 2, wherein the mating faces of the first and second brace-halves comprise interlocking features selected from a tongue-and-groove profile, a stepped rabbet joint, or dowel-receiving apertures.

**Claim 6.** The frame of claim 1, wherein the support brace defines a hollow interior cavity formed jointly by a recess in the first frame half-shell and a corresponding recess in the second frame half-shell.

**Claim 7.** The frame of claim 1, wherein the first and second frame half-shells are formed of cast aluminum alloy, cast magnesium alloy, stamped steel, or fiber-reinforced composite material.

---

## Advantages of the Invention

- Reduced part count through integral brace formation within each half-shell;
- Simplified manufacturing via single-operation casting or forming of each half-shell, inclusive of brace geometry;
- Improved structural continuity at brace junctions by eliminating separate attachment interfaces;
- Enhanced design flexibility, permitting the separating surface to be routed through multiple structural zones as needed for optimized load paths;
- Potential weight reduction through hollow brace construction enabled by complementary half-shell recesses.

---

*This summary is presented for illustrative purposes as a formal patent specification abstract and detailed description template, subject to refinement of claim scope, drawings, and reference numerals in a complete filing.*

# BICYCLE FRAME ASSEMBLY WITH BONDED SHELL CONSTRUCTION

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to bicycle frame structures, and more particularly to a bicycle frame formed from a plurality of shell members joined along a parting line to define an integrated monocoque-style frame body incorporating receiving areas for principal frame components and an integrally formed rear fork structure.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Conventional bicycle frames are typically constructed from discrete tubular members joined at their respective ends through welding, brazing, or adhesive lug connections. While such constructions have achieved widespread commercial acceptance, they suffer from certain drawbacks, including stress concentrations at joint interfaces, limitations in achievable geometries, increased manufacturing complexity arising from the need to align and join multiple discrete tubes, and constraints on material selection imposed by joining methodologies.

There exists a need in the art for a bicycle frame construction that reduces the number of discrete joints, permits greater design freedom in frame geometry, and facilitates manufacture from a broader range of materials, including composite materials, while maintaining or improving structural performance characteristics such as stiffness-to-weight ratio, fatigue resistance, and impact tolerance.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

In accordance with the present invention, there is provided a bicycle frame comprising a first shell half and a second shell half, each shell half extending substantially along the length of the frame and being configured to mate with the other shell half along a parting line to define an enclosed or partially enclosed frame body. Each shell half comprises complementary formations that, when the shell halves are joined, cooperatively define a plurality of receiving areas configured to accept and retain principal bicycle components, including a head tube receiving area configured to receive a handlebar steering tube assembly, a bottom bracket receiving area configured to receive a bottom bracket assembly, and a seat tube receiving area configured to receive a seatpost or seat tube member.

The frame further comprises a rear fork structure extending rearwardly from the frame body, the rear fork structure being formed integrally with, or joined to, the shell halves and comprising a pair of stay members configured to extend to and support a rear wheel axle.

In certain embodiments, the shell halves are joined along the parting line by an adhesive bonding process, a welding process, a fastening process, or combinations thereof. In certain embodiments, the shell halves are formed from a fiber-reinforced composite material, a metallic material, or combinations thereof.

The first shell half **12** and the second shell half **14** each comprise an inner surface **24** and an outer surface **26**. In certain embodiments, the interior cavity **28** may be hollow so as to reduce overall frame weight. In other embodiments, the interior cavity **28** may be partially or wholly filled with a core material, such as a foam core, a honeycomb core, or a lattice structure, to enhance structural rigidity.

Along the parting line **20**, the first shell half **12** and the second shell half **14** may comprise complementary mating formations **30**, such as tongue-and-groove formations, overlapping flange formations, or stepped-lap formations, configured to facilitate alignment of the shell halves **12**, **14** during assembly and to increase the bonding surface area at the parting line **20**.

In still further embodiments, the shell halves **12**, **14** may be joined by mechanical fasteners, such as rivets, bolts, or clips, either alone or in combination with adhesive bonding.

The shell halves **12**, **14** may be formed from any material or combination of materials suitable for bicycle frame construction, including without limitation carbon fiber-reinforced polymer, glass fiber-reinforced polymer, aramid fiber-reinforced polymer, aluminum, titanium, steel, magnesium, or combinations thereof. In embodiments employing composite materials, the shell halves **12**, **14** may be formed by a molding process, such as compression molding, resin transfer molding, or vacuum-assisted resin transfer molding, wherein fiber-reinforced material is laid up within a mold cavity corresponding to the desired shell geometry and subsequently cured.

# PATENT DISCLOSURE

## TITLE OF INVENTION
**HOLLOW-CONSTRUCTED VEHICLE FRAME ASSEMBLY WITH BILATERAL REAR SUPPORT BRACE STRUCTURE AND UNIFIED PARTING SURFACE CONFIGURATION**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to frame structures for two-wheeled vehicles, including motorcycles and bicycles, and more particularly to a hollow support frame construction incorporating left and right rear support braces joined along a common separating (parting) surface, providing improved structural rigidity, reduced weight, and simplified manufacturing.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Conventional motorcycle and bicycle frames are typically constructed using welded tubular steel or aluminum members, or cast/forged solid sections joined at discrete points. These approaches present several drawbacks:

1. **Weight inefficiency** — solid or thick-walled tubular members add unnecessary mass without proportional gains in strength.
2. **Manufacturing complexity** — multi-piece welded assemblies require extensive fixturing, welding operations, and post-weld machining, increasing production cost and introducing potential weld-defect failure points.
3. **Inconsistent load paths** — traditional frames often lack a unified structural surface, causing stress concentrations at joints between the main frame body and rear support braces.
4. **Assembly misalignment** — separately manufactured left/right rear braces frequently suffer from dimensional variance, requiring additional alignment jigs during final assembly.

There exists a need for a frame design that reduces mass through hollow construction while maintaining structural integrity, and that allows the main frame and rear support braces to be manufactured and joined using a shared, precisely defined parting surface to ensure repeatable alignment and load transfer.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention provides a **hollow support frame assembly** for a motorcycle or bicycle comprising:

- A **main frame body** defining an internal hollow cavity extending along at least a portion of its length, formed preferably by casting, hydroforming, or split-shell fabrication;
- A **left rear support brace** and a **right rear support brace**, each extending rearward from the main frame body toward a rear axle mounting region, each brace likewise possessing an internal hollow cavity;
- A **shared separating surface** (parting surface) common to the main frame body, the left rear support brace, and the right rear support brace, wherein said surface defines the mating interface along which the frame components are divided during manufacture (e.g., mold-half separation, die-cast split line, or two-shell weld/bond line) and subsequently rejoined during assembly.

The shared separating surface ensures that the main frame and both left and right braces originate from a common geometric reference plane, thereby guaranteeing dimensional consistency, simplifying tooling, and enabling continuous internal hollow passages that may extend from the main frame into each rear brace without interruption — improving both weight reduction and torsional stiffness.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

### 1. General Frame Structure

Referring to the frame assembly (10), the invention comprises a main frame body (12) which houses the primary structural cavity (14). The main frame body (12) extends from a head tube region (16), through a central spine or backbone section (18), to a seat/rear mounting region (20).

The main frame body (12) is formed from two complementary shell halves — a first shell half (12a) and a second shell half (12b) — joined along the shared separating surface (30). This separating surface (30) is a continuous geometric plane (or contoured surface, in non-planar embodiments) that defines the boundary along which the frame was originally split for mold release, forging die separation, or shell stamping.

### 2. Left and Right Rear Support Braces

Extending rearward from the main frame body (12) at the seat/rear mounting region (20) are:

- **Left rear support brace (22)** — extending along the left side of the vehicle toward the left rear axle mount (24);
- **Right rear support brace (26)** — extending along the right side of the vehicle toward the right rear axle mount (28), forming a mirrored bilateral pair.

Each of the left rear support brace (22) and right rear support brace (26) is likewise hollow, defining internal cavities (22a) and (26a) respectively, which may be fluidly or structurally continuous with the primary structural cavity (14) of the main frame body (12), or separated by internal ribbing/bulkheads (32) for localized stiffness tuning.

Critically, each rear support brace (22, 26) is formed such that its own shell-half split line coincides with — and is coplanar or contour-matched to — the shared separating surface (30) of the main frame body (12). This means:

- The **first shell half (12a)** of the main frame integrally extends into the **outer shell half** of both the left brace (22) and right brace (26);
- The **second shell half (12b)** of the main frame integrally extends into the **inner shell half** of both braces;

such that only two shell components (12a, 12b) — rather than six or more discrete parts — are required to form the entire main-frame-plus-bilateral-brace structure.

### 3. Shared Separating Surface — Structural and Manufacturing Advantages

The shared separating surface (30) provides:

- **(a) Unified Tooling Reference:** A single die/mold parting geometry serves the main frame and both rear braces simultaneously, reducing tooling cost and eliminating cumulative tolerance stack-up between separately split components.
- **(b) Continuous Load Path:** Because the split line is common across all three structural elements, the joint (weld, adhesive bond, or mechanical fastening) between shell halves lies along a single continuous seam, rather than at discrete brace-to-frame junctions. This reduces stress risers at the transition between the main frame and each brace.
- **(c) Simplified Joining Process:** The two shell halves (12a, 12b) — each carrying integral left-brace and right-brace half-sections — may be joined in a single operation (e.g., friction stir welding, adhesive bonding, laser welding, or mechanical clinching along the full seam), rather than requiring separate joining operations for the frame and each brace.
- **(d) Internal Cavity Continuity:** The hollow cavity (14) of the main frame may extend uninterrupted into cavities (22a, 26a) of each brace, permitting internal routing of wiring harnesses, brake/hydraulic lines, or airflow (for cooling) without external routing hardware.

### 4. Alternative Embodiments

- **Embodiment A:** The separating surface (30) is a single flat plane bisecting the frame symmetrically (left-right), suitable for simple two-shell die casting.
- **Embodiment B:** The separating surface (30) is a contoured, non-planar surface following the natural curvature of the frame's load paths, optimized via topology analysis, suitable for hydroformed or superplastic-formed sheet construction.
- **Embodiment C:** Internal bulkheads (32) are positioned at the junction between the main frame body (12) and each rear brace (22, 26) to locally reinforce the shared seam while preserving overall hollow construction.
- **Embodiment D:** The left and right rear support braces (22, 26) further include reinforcing ribs (34) integrally formed within the hollow cavity during the shell-forming process, positioned along the shared separating surface for maximal stiffness-to-weight contribution.

---

## CLAIMS (Representative)

**1.** A frame assembly for a motorcycle or bicycle, comprising:
a main frame body defining an internal hollow cavity;
a left rear support brace extending rearward from the main frame body, said left rear support brace defining an internal hollow cavity;
a right rear support brace extending rearward from the main frame body, said right rear support brace defining an internal hollow cavity;
wherein the main frame body, the left rear support brace, and the right rear support brace are each formed from a first shell half and a second shell half joined along a shared separating surface common to all three structural elements.

**2.** The frame assembly of claim 1, wherein the internal hollow cavity of the main frame body is continuous with the internal hollow cavities of the left and right rear support braces.

**3.** The frame assembly of claim 1, wherein the shared separating surface is substantially planar.

**4.** The frame assembly of claim 1, wherein the shared separating surface is a contoured, non-planar surface following the structural load path of the frame assembly.

**5.** The frame assembly of claim 1, further comprising one or more internal bulkheads disposed at the junction between the main frame body and each of the left and right rear support braces.

**6.** The frame assembly of claim 1, wherein the first shell half and second shell half are joined by a process selected from the group consisting of: welding, adhesive bonding, mechanical fastening, and friction stir welding.

**7.** The frame assembly of claim 1, further comprising integrally formed reinforcing ribs within the internal hollow cavities of the left and right rear support braces.

**8.** A method of manufacturing a vehicle frame assembly, comprising:
forming a first shell half comprising a main frame outer section, a left brace outer section, and a right brace outer section;
forming a second shell half comprising a main frame inner section, a left brace inner section, and a right brace inner section;
joining the first shell half to the second shell half along a single continuous shared separating surface to form a unified hollow frame structure comprising a main frame body and bilateral rear support braces.

---

## ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION

- Reduced part count (two shells vs. multiple discrete tubes/braces)
- Reduced overall frame weight via hollow construction
- Improved structural continuity and reduced stress concentration at frame-to-brace junctions
- Simplified tooling and assembly via unified parting geometry
- Potential for internal routing of cables/hydraulic lines through continuous cavities
- Adaptable to casting, hydroforming, or composite shell-molding manufacturing processes

---

*This disclosure is intended to support subsequent formal patent application drafting, including formal claims, drawings (FIGS. 1–6 illustrating frame isometric view, exploded shell-half view, cross-sections through main frame and each brace, and parting-surface contour maps), and an abstract in accordance with applicable patent office formatting requirements.*

The invention relates to a frame for a two-wheeled vehicle, and more particularly to a frame construction comprising two shell halves which are joined together to form a hollow cavity extending along at least a portion of the frame structure. The invention further relates to a frame of this type in which the two shell halves are configured such that the parting plane defined by their mutual joining extends through both of the rear wheel support struts, such that each strut is likewise composed of two half-shell portions that together form part of the overall shell construction.
